title: Cloud Security Posture Management
summary: Cloud security posture management is the continuous discovery, assessment and remediation of configuration risk across cloud accounts, covering identity grants, network exposure, storage permissions, encryption settings, logging coverage and compliance against a chosen baseline. A CSPM capability connects to provider APIs with read-only credentials, enumerates every resource in scope, evaluates each against policy rules, and reports the drift between intended and actual state with enough context to prioritise. Its output is deliberately different from a vulnerability scanner: rather than finding flaws in code, it finds misconfiguration in deployed infrastructure, which is the dominant cause of cloud incidents. Effective implementations depend on several disciplines. Rules must be mapped to recognised benchmarks so that findings carry external meaning, and they must be tuned so that each alert corresponds to a real risk, because unmanaged volume produces alert fatigue and silent suppression. Ownership has to route to the team able to fix the resource, and the tool must distinguish misconfiguration that is exploitable now from latent risk. Coverage itself is a risk area, since accounts and regions excluded from scanning are invisible, and a new account created outside the pipeline arrives unmonitored. Mature programmes treat posture findings as code defects, feeding them back into templates and guardrails so the same mistake cannot be redeployed.
objectives: You will be able to explain what CSPM evaluates and how it differs from vulnerability scanning, CSPP and cloud infrastructure entitlement work.
You will be able to map posture findings to a recognised benchmark and justify the priority assigned to each.
You will be able to tune noisy rules without suppressing genuine exposure, and identify the tradeoff each suppression introduces.
You will be able to detect coverage gaps such as unscanned accounts, regions and newly created subscriptions.
You will be able to write a posture finding report that a platform team can act on without further triage.

beginner.definition: Cloud security posture management is the practice of continuously checking your cloud accounts for risky settings. It looks at who has access, what is exposed to the internet, how storage is shared, and whether logging and encryption are on. It compares what you have with what you intended.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most cloud incidents start with a simple setting mistake, not clever malware. Someone leaves a storage bucket open, or grants far more access than needed. These gaps are invisible in code review because they live in the live account. Posture management finds them early, before an attacker does, and shows your team what to fix first.
howItWorks: You connect the tool to your cloud account with read-only access, so it can look but not change.
It lists every resource, such as storage buckets, virtual machines, accounts and network rules.
Each resource is compared against written rules that describe a safe setting.
Anything that breaks a rule becomes a finding, with a severity and the reason it matters.
The finding is sent to the team that owns that resource so they can correct it.
The best teams then fix the template that created it, so the same mistake cannot return.
beginner.example: Imagine a large block of flats. The landlord checks the building once a month: are any doors unlocked, are windows open, are fire exits blocked? Nobody broke in, but the survey still finds real risk. Cloud posture management is that monthly walk-through, except it runs continuously and checks every flat at once.
takeaways: Posture management finds configuration mistakes in your live cloud accounts, not in code.
Connect it with read-only access and fix noisy rules so alerts stay useful.
Feed findings back into templates so the same mistake is never deployed again.

exercises.title: Cloud Security Posture Management - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Cloud Security Posture Management - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Cloud Security Posture Management - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Cloud Security Posture Management - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
